beats.idea: Seller refuses grain; barter stalls
beats.relation_note: Cross the offered grain at नहीं; add a question mark between buyer and shoes at कैसे.
beats.shows: Seller rejects grain; shoes remain; question mark appears
beats.template_note: Buyer offers grain for shoes; seller looks, shakes head at नहीं, and a cross lands on the grain. Shoes stay with seller; question mark appears at कैसे.

beats.idea: Barter leaves wheat plus acquired cloth
beats.relation_note: Show initial stock, direct exchange, then final holdings.
beats.shows: Wheat exchanged for cloth; eight kilograms remain
beats.template_note: Start with 10 kg wheat; separate 2 kg on '2 kg', exchange it for 1 metre cloth on 'देकर', and show 8 kg wheat plus cloth on 'बचा'. Do not add an unscripted negotiation.

beats.idea: Barter is direct exchange without money
beats.relation_note: Goods move directly in opposite directions; a separate crossed-out money intermediary indicates what is absent.
beats.shows: Wheat and cloth swap; money intermediary crossed out
beats.template_note: Owners offer wheat and cloth, indicate mutual wants, then swap directly. Reveal and cross out a separate money intermediary on 'बिना'.

beats.idea: Selling then buying with money is not barter
beats.relation_note: Two linked transactions involve a wheat seller, a wheat buyer and a separate cloth seller; cross only the barter label on 'नहीं'.
beats.shows: Wheat sold; money buys cloth; barter label crossed
beats.template_note: Chain handovers: seller gives wheat to wheat buyer and receives money; that seller then gives the money to a different cloth seller and receives cloth.

beats.idea: Direct exchange identifies barter
beats.relation_note: Tick the direct goods-for-goods exchange as the identifying barter pattern.
beats.shows: Direct wheat–cloth swap receives a tick
beats.template_note: Replay the direct swap briefly, then tick the paired exchange; no money or intermediary appears.

beats.idea: No money does not mean free
beats.relation_note: Cross out money, while retaining the wheat-for-cloth exchange.
beats.shows: Crossed money; wheat and cloth swap hands
beats.template_note: Show wheat offered and cloth returned; no cash leg.

beats.idea: Services can be bartered too
beats.relation_note: Repairing a bicycle and receiving grain form the service-for-goods exchange.
beats.shows: Mechanic repairs bicycle; owner hands over grain
beats.template_note: Mechanic repairs bicycle with spanner; owner gives grain in return.

beats.idea: Both parties decide the value
beats.relation_note: Both parties approve the proposed wheat-to-cloth exchange, rather than the seller deciding alone.
beats.shows: Wheat–cloth proposal between two nodding traders
beats.template_note: Both traders inspect the exchange proposal and nod; ticks appear beside both.

beats.idea: An agreed example, not a fixed rate
beats.relation_note: Pair a wheat sack marked 2 kg with cloth measured at 1 metre inside this pair's agreement.
beats.shows: Two-kilogram wheat swaps for one-metre cloth
beats.template_note: Both approve, then swap the measured quantities; frame as this agreement only.

beats.idea: Barter includes goods and services without money
beats.relation_note: Group goods-for-goods and service-for-goods examples inside barter, with money crossed outside.
beats.shows: Barter box contains goods swap and repair exchange
beats.template_note: Recap the two already-demonstrated processes as grouped examples, not a new transaction.

beats.idea: Direct, moneyless, mutually agreed exchange
beats.relation_note: Both approve, then exchange directly; money remains crossed out.
beats.shows: Direct wheat–cloth swap; crossed money; two ticks
beats.template_note: Show reciprocal direct transfers, cross money on बिना पैसे, and tick both parties on हाँ.

beats.idea: Barter survives from early civilizations
beats.shows: Ancient barter crowd; arrow to neighbours swapping goods
beats.template_note: Neighbours offer vegetables and grain, check mutual interest, then exchange; connect this scene to the early-civilizations scene.

beats.idea: Matching needs enable moneyless exchange
beats.shows: Matching wants lead to goods swapping hands
beats.template_note: Each neighbour's thought bubble shows the other's goods; both nod, then swap goods without money changing hands.

beats.idea: Money and barter can coexist
beats.shows: Barter and money exchanges share today's timeline
beats.template_note: The point is coexistence, not transaction steps; show parallel static exchange scenes, neither crossed out.

beats.idea: Barter became limited, not extinct
beats.shows: Many barter pairs before; few barter pairs today
beats.template_note: A qualitative prevalence comparison, not a counted population or an exchange process.

beats.idea: Wheat हर cloth seller को नहीं चाहिए
beats.relation_note: पहले seller का refusal, फिर दूसरे seller की acceptance दिखाएँ।
beats.shows: पहला seller wheat ठुकराता; दूसरा cloth देता
beats.template_note: पहले seller की oil चाह दिखाएँ; 'मना' पर wheat पर cross। दूसरे की wheat चाह दिखाकर 'मान' पर tick और 2 kg wheat–1 metre cloth swap।

beats.idea: Barter में दोनों की चाह मिलनी चाहिए
beats.relation_note: दोनों चाह मिलने वाला pair और केवल एक चाह मिलने वाला pair समान slots में रखें।
beats.shows: दोतरफा चाह बनाम केवल एकतरफा चाह
beats.template_note: यह सफल swap की शर्त समझाता है; नया transaction नहीं।

beats.idea: Money से बेचने और खरीदने वाले अलग
beats.relation_note: Accepted money wheat buyer और cloth seller की चाहों को match करने की जरूरत हटाता है।
beats.shows: Wheat बेचकर पैसा; पैसे देकर cloth
beats.template_note: Farmer wheat buyer को wheat देता और money लेता है; फिर अलग cloth seller को वही money देकर cloth लेता है। Cloth seller की wheat चाह पर cross, money पर tick; रकम न गढ़ें।

beats.idea: अलग ratios और अविभाज्य गाय
beats.relation_note: ज्ञात wheat–cloth ratio के साथ गाय का अनिर्धारित ratio और छोटी खरीद का प्रश्न दिखाएँ।
beats.shows: Wheat–cloth ratio; अखंड गाय पर प्रश्नचिह्न
beats.template_note: Exchange ratio एक तय शर्त है, completed swap नहीं; गाय बाँटने का प्रश्न है, वास्तविक विभाजन नहीं दिखाएँ।

beats.idea: वही अनाज, कम cloth purchasing power
beats.relation_note: 10 kg अनाज की quantity और quality स्थिर रखें; उसके बदले मिलने वाला cloth 2 metres से 1 metre करें।
beats.shows: वही अनाज; cloth बराबरी दो से एक
beats.template_note: अब 2 metres cloth handover और बाद में तय quality के 10 kg grain देने का receipt दिखाएँ। बाद में वही grain लौटे; valuation inset में 10 kg स्थिर और cloth equivalent 2 metres से 1 metre हो। अतिरिक्त cloth handover न दिखाएँ।

beats.idea: Barter में मूल्य, विभाजन, भंडारण और repayment की बाधाएँ
beats.shows: Conflicting scales; whole cow; rot; shrinking repayment basket
beats.template_note: चार conceptual cause-effect reveals, कोई completed exchange नहीं: ratios पर गाय-अनाज और गाय-कपड़ा के असंगत तुला-दृश्य; indivisibility पर पूरी गाय और विभाजन पर रोक; सड़े पर भंडार का अनाज खराब; बाद में पर calendar के दोनों ओर समान repayment grain sack, लेकिन भविष्य में उससे मिलने वाला goods basket छोटा।

beats.idea: Money में debt स्पष्ट, purchasing power अनिश्चित
beats.shows: Same debt, unequal baskets; wants versus quantities
beats.template_note: Debt लिखना एक conceptual advantage है, cheque transaction नहीं। Ledger की वही rupee entry आज और बाद में रखें; fixed नहीं पर बराबर cash के सामने अलग basket sizes दिखाएँ। जरूरतें मिलना पर दोनों traders के thought bubbles में दूसरे की वस्तु और ticks; quantities पर अलग balance scale तथा agreement का question mark।

beats.idea: Barter की बाधाएँ matching से repayment तक
beats.shows: Matching, valuation, division, storage, repayment obstacle chain
beats.template_note: यह पिछली कठिनाइयों का recap है, वास्तविक barter swap नहीं। Arrow-linked row में matching के traders, valuation की scale, indivisible cow, spoiled grain और calendar सहित repayment basket दिखाएँ; repayment पर अंतिम obstacle उभरे।

beats.idea: Barter first; payment methods evolve
beats.relation_note: Highlight the first stage, then trace the existing gallery arrows to indicate changing payment methods.
beats.shows: Crossed coin; wheat–cloth swap; first stage highlighted
beats.template_note: Owners offer wheat and cloth and consider each other’s goods; a coin appears at ‘पैसा’ and is crossed out at ‘नहीं’; goods swap directly at ‘barter’. At ‘बदलाव’, trace the gallery’s arrows without adding money between the barter participants.

beats.idea: Salt mediates two exchanges
beats.shows: Wheat buys salt; salt then buys cloth
beats.template_note: Two successive swaps: farmer gives 2 kg wheat for 1 kg salt, then all that salt for 1 metre cloth. Keep salt visibly moving between transactions.

beats.idea: Commodity money bridges different wants
beats.shows: Salt bridges wheat and cloth; stage two highlighted
beats.template_note: Recap the preceding exchange as a static salt bridge, not another transaction; add salt, cattle and shells at stage 2.

beats.idea: Metal coins pay; remaining coins can be counted
beats.shows: Five coins; two pay; three remain
beats.template_note: Show five matching silver coins, move two to the seller and 5 kg grain to the buyer, leaving three coins. Then highlight stage 3 with gold and silver coins.

beats.idea: Standard coins are countable commodities
beats.shows: Matching coins counted inside commodity money group
beats.template_note: Count matching coins individually without adding a new spoken total; equal-weight scale and matching purity marks show standardisation. Enclose gold and silver coins within commodity money.

beats.idea: Notes pay by denomination and return change
beats.shows: ₹500 paid; goods and ₹200 returned
beats.template_note: Buyer pays ₹500 for ₹300 goods and receives ₹200 change. Highlight stage 4 and the note's printed ₹500 denomination, not its paper material.

beats.idea: Notes carry value without metal's weight
beats.shows: Easy note carrying versus burdensome metal sack
beats.template_note: Compare a person carrying a light note easily with a person straining under a heavy sack of metal coins; do not invent a numerical equivalence.

beats.idea: Cheque transfers existing bank deposits
beats.shows: Cheque settles; payer falls, shopkeeper rises equally
beats.template_note: Show payer ₹10,000 and shopkeeper ₹2,000; write and submit ₹1,500 cheque, then update balances to ₹8,500 and ₹3,500. Highlight stage 5; equal debit and credit show no new money created.

beats.idea: Digital instructions transfer account money
beats.shows: Phone scans QR; ₹300 moves between accounts
beats.template_note: Start with buyer ₹2,000 and shopkeeper ₹5,000. Phone scans shop QR, displays ₹300 paid, and seller receives ₹300; balances become ₹1,700 and ₹5,300. Highlight stage 6 with UPI, net banking and cards; no paper changes hands.

beats.idea: Intermediaries ease exchange; UPI moves existing deposits
beats.shows: Money bridges trade; UPI shifts deposits, total unchanged
beats.template_note: First show money bridging buyer and seller without mutual goods-matching. At UPI, scan the seller's QR; buyer deposit decreases as seller deposit increases equally. Show paid and received confirmations; hold their combined total fixed at नहीं बनाता.

beats.idea: Forms coexist; cards need not contain money
beats.shows: Forms coexist; account-linked card versus stored-value card
beats.template_note: No payment action is narrated. Keep notes, coins and phone together; contrast a card linked to an external bank balance with a stored-value card. Avoid portraying all cards as empty or all as money containers.

beats.idea: Recall the book's six-stage ordering
beats.shows: Six numbered money forms highlight along arrows
beats.template_note: A sequence recap, not a barter transaction. Highlight the book's numbered panels on barter, commodity, metallic, paper, bank and digital respectively; retain earlier panels.

beats.idea: Two sources of payment value
beats.shows: Salt ₹20 and note ₹500 beside payment arrows
beats.template_note: Paired exchanges: salt packet accepted as payment at assumed ₹20 value; ₹500 note handed over to settle ₹500.

beats.idea: Utility survives loss of monetary acceptance
beats.shows: Refused salt still cooks; paper lacks ₹500 worth
beats.template_note: Seller refuses salt as payment; then salt moves beside a cooking pot and resale tag with variable price. Contrast note material with face value; cross a redemption-receipt symbol, not a valid note’s purchasing power.

beats.idea: Material versus external backing
beats.shows: Gold material versus note with trust and law

beats.idea: Material worth is not purchasing power
beats.shows: Salt cooks; negligible paper value, intact purchasing power
beats.template_note: Static paired states distinguish nonmonetary utility from purchasing power; no transaction is enacted.

beats.idea: Commodity examples versus monetary claims
beats.shows: Commodity group beside notes and bank claim icons
beats.template_note: Examples populate two groups as named; no narrated numerical count. Link account holder to bank through a payment-claim document, not stored physical goods.

beats.idea: Acceptance depends on onward spending
beats.shows: Salt refused outside; rupees reach the next shop
beats.template_note: Outside seller examines salt, shakes head, and cross lands on salt at मना. A following arrow chain shows accepted rupees usable at another shop; local salt retains a utility cue.

beats.idea: Small payments and carrying burden
beats.shows: Bulky commodities versus small payments; cutting note crossed
beats.template_note: Show static difficulty dividing a cow and carrying salt versus small denominations and a phone. Cross scissors beside the note; do not enact destruction as divisibility.

beats.idea: UPI transfers an existing balance
beats.shows: Bullion opposite notes, balances and UPI transfer
beats.template_note: After paired examples appear, phone scans QR; paid and received confirmations follow. Show linked bank balances decreasing and increasing equally, with no separate UPI money pile; no invented spoken amount.

beats.idea: Law, trust and practical usability differ
beats.shows: Law settles debt; trust, portability, durability contrasted
beats.template_note: Stamped legal-tender scroll accompanies payment from debtor to creditor; debt ledger closes. Separate onward-shop arrow conveys trust. Then highlight small-payment, carrying and durability comparisons, with digital balance linked to technology.

beats.idea: Avoid four misleading equivalences
beats.shows: Moving prices; crossed equivalences; disconnected phone, intact balance
beats.template_note: Cycle price tags on the same commodity. Cross backing-equals-gold-redemption and every-coin-equals-material-worth links. Break the phone connection while its bank balance remains visibly unchanged.

beats.idea: Utility differs from money; commodities deteriorate
beats.shows: Utility unequal payment; sick cow and damp salt
beats.template_note: Separate cooking utility from monetary value using an unequal sign. Then show healthy cow becoming sick and dry salt becoming damp and clumped.

beats.idea: Salt has value beyond payment
beats.relation_note: Exchange first; if onward payment fails, use the received salt in cooking.
beats.shows: Grain exchanged for salt; rejected payment becomes seasoning
beats.template_note: At 'grain', exchange grain for exactly two salt packets; at 'न चलें', the next trader refuses salt as payment; at 'खाना', the seller adds that salt to a cooking pot. Keep the refusal cross confined to the payment attempt.

beats.idea: Salt has value beyond payment
beats.shows: Same salt: payment handover beside cooking pot
beats.template_note: Split view: salt handed over as payment; salt sprinkled into cooking pot.

beats.idea: Usefulness and purchasing power are insufficient separately
beats.shows: Salt passes both tests; note classification crossed
beats.template_note: Payment is a criterion here, not a narrated transaction. Reveal matched payment and outside-use slots; cross only the note's commodity-money label on नहीं.

beats.idea: Outside-payment usefulness is essential
beats.shows: Salt payment beside salt used in cooking
beats.template_note: Recap of two uses, not a new transaction.

beats.idea: Salt ke regions; cattle ki communities
beats.relation_note: Salt connects to geographic regions; cattle connects to a herding-community vignette rather than a map pin.
beats.shows: Salt beside maps; cattle beside herders
beats.template_note: Historical use is stated; no counting or transfer is narrated.

beats.idea: Cowries: regions aur payment mein acceptance
beats.relation_note: Locate cowrie use in India, China and Africa; finish with a recipient accepting the shells.
beats.shows: Palm-held cowries, three regions, recipient acceptance tick
beats.template_note: Show recipient examining cowries, nodding, then a tick on स्वीकार.

beats.idea: Tea bricks aur tobacco ke alag regions
beats.relation_note: Pair compressed tea with Central Asia and Tibet; pair dried tobacco leaves with Colonial America. Contrast tea brick with a crossed-out construction brick.
beats.shows: Tea brick and tobacco beside their regions
beats.image_wanted: compressed tea brick dried tobacco leaves
beats.template_note: बनेगा introduces an identification question, not a narrated manufacturing process.

beats.idea: Three quantities have equal assumed value
beats.shows: Equal-value goods; farmer's thought bubble contains cloth

beats.idea: Salt bridges grain and cloth exchanges
beats.shows: Grain swaps for salt; salt swaps for cloth
beats.template_note: Two successive swaps: farmer gives 10 kg grain to salt trader and receives 2 kg salt; farmer gives that entire salt bundle to cloth seller and receives 2 metres cloth. End with cloth alone in farmer's holdings and visibly empty grain and salt slots.

beats.idea: Salt bridges mismatched wants
beats.shows: Buyer→salt→farmer→salt→cloth seller; grain and cloth return
beats.template_note: Buyer gives salt for farmer's grain; farmer passes salt to cloth seller for cloth. Show farmer's own salt-use need crossed out, then remove the direct buyer-to-cloth requirement at 'हटी'.

beats.idea: Commodities retain uses beyond payment
beats.shows: Salt beside cooking; cattle livelihood; tea, tobacco demand
beats.template_note: Uses and demand are illustrated associations, not a narrated transaction process.

beats.idea: Usefulness plus local acceptance enables exchange
beats.shows: Use plus community ticks→exchange; commodities before coins
beats.template_note: Show conditions enabling exchange, not an invented transaction: usefulness and community acceptance jointly feed exchange arrows. Outside the community retain a question mark; add commodities-before-coins timeline, then disconnect usefulness alone from acceptance at 'अकेला'.

beats.idea: Spoilage leaves less grain for later payment
beats.shows: 100 kg → 90 kg; future grain payment questioned
beats.template_note: Show 100 kg stored grain; 10 kg spoils, leaving 90 kg usable; arrow to grain payment between payer and recipient with question mark.

beats.idea: Commodity money has physical limitations
beats.relation_note: Group five pictured limitations under commodity money.
beats.shows: Spoiled grain; cows, sack, measures show limitations
beats.template_note: Names limitations rather than narrating a transaction or process.

beats.idea: Variation and missing standards complicate trade
beats.relation_note: Different cow sizes and health show nonuniformity; absent weight and quality rules lead to repeated inspection and bargaining.
beats.shows: Unequal cows; absent rules trigger checks and bargaining
beats.template_note: Compare cows, show weight and quality rules, then absent rules causing repeated inspection and exchanged price offers.

beats.idea: Handling problems add payment and storage costs
beats.relation_note: Three aligned chains connect indivisible cow to small-payment difficulty, spoiling grain to storage cost, and heavy sack to transport cost.
beats.shows: Cow, spoiling grain, heavy sack cause extra costs
beats.template_note: Keep cow intact against small portions; grain spoils in storage; porter loads heavy sack; expense coins accumulate.

beats.idea: Limitations differ across commodities
beats.relation_note: Compare divisibility of grain and cow, then spoilage of food and shells; cross only the universal claim ‘सभी’.
beats.shows: Grain divides; cow stays whole; shells outlast food
beats.template_note: Split grain into portions while cow remains whole; food deteriorates while shells stay unchanged; cross ‘सभी’ on that word.

beats.idea: Handling needs favour durable measured metal
beats.relation_note: Separate easier matching from unresolved handling; handling problems point toward durable metal units with measured weights.
beats.shows: Matching tick; handling burdens point toward weighed metal
beats.template_note: Summarizes a causal advantage, not a narrated exchange or metal-making process.
